transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-08-13
- Time: 16:00 UTC (45-60 window including intro)
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Rahul (Redwood SE), Jenna (Sparrow Head of IT), Tom (Procurement), Priya (Security)

Summary:
Quick procurement/technical alignment to decide pilot pricing tier, confirm MSA/DPA redline owners, and validate connectivity/KMS requirements for a 3-month pilot. High focus on private data handling, SSO/KMS, and SLA expectations for burst vs baseline throughput.

Topics:
1) Pilot scope & targets
2) MSA/DPA redlines and timelines
3) SLA & pricing options (hosted vs dedicated)
4) Network/KMS/SSO connectivity plan
5) Next steps & owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we've got about 50 minutes today, we'll run through the scope for the pilot and then get the procurement/legal items lined up. Rahul's gonna cover the tech bits.
[00:18] Jenna Morales: Great, thanks. We have Tom and Priya on as well, Tom will handle the PO and payment path, Priya for security. Quick note — timeline is kinda tight, we'd like pilot live by mid-September.
[00:30] Tom Li: Yep, internal approvals are a two-step but we can expedite if pricing and SLA are clear.
[00:36] Rahul Patel: Cool. For context, the pilot target is about 50 qps at peak for chat generation, 10M tokens/day estimated, mix of short and medium sequences. We'll propose Redwood Dedicated reserved pool for predictable latency, with fallback to hosted for overflow.
[00:52] Priya Singh: When you say Dedicated, is customer-managed VPC available? We need the private deployment option or at least VPC peering and CMK for keys.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Yes, we offer Private deployment and VPC options. For pilots we typically do VPC peering to a test environment, KMS integration with customer-managed keys is supported — though we need to check the exact HSM/KMS provider compatibility.
[01:17] Jenna Morales: Ok, compatibility with our key vendor (HashiCorp Vault in our case) is a must. Also we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM and at-rest encryption certs.
[01:29] Rahul Patel: Noted. From the runtime side, we can enable audit forwarding and token-level logging to your syslog endpoint. There may be some PII redaction configs; we'll need Priya's list of data classes.
[01:42] Priya Singh: I'll send the data-class matrix. Also, SOC 2 is fine but we need an attestation on data residency — our customers in EMEA require logs not to leave region. Is region pinning possible for the pilot?
[01:55] Maya Chen: Yes, we can pin region to eu-west-1 for the pilot nodes. There's a note: cross-region fallback will be disabled for compliance. That will affect burst capacity but we can size accordingly.
[02:08] Tom Li: About the MSA/DPA — our legal team flagged a few clauses: indemnities, data processing addendum specifics, and liability caps. Can you run through typical vendor concessions?
[02:22] Maya Chen: Sure. For most enterprise pilots we accept DPA with standard SCCs, we can accept vendor-side data processing limits and usually keep liability cap aligned to fees for 12 months. MSA redlines are fine but we generally push back on unlimited indemnities. We'll share a redline summary.
[02:38] Jenna Morales: Also curious on retention windows — logs retained by Redwood for 90 days by default? We need 30 days max for pilot.
[02:47] Rahul Patel: We can change log retention for the pilot to 30 days, but for production we recommend longer for diagnostics. It's a config in the console.
[02:56] Priya Singh: Regarding SSO, we use SAML-based SSO with Okta. We'll need admin RBAC and SCIM user provisioning.
[03:06] Maya Chen: Okta SAML + SCIM is supported. We'll need a provisioning SAML metadata and an admin user to set up. Rahul will send a step-by-step runbook.
[03:16] Rahul Patel: I'll drop the runbook. Also network — we prefer customers provision a test VPC and establish VPC peering; alternatively, we can do secure peering via transit. For Sparrow, peering is cleaner.
[03:28] Tom Li: On pricing — we need clarity between billed tokens vs reserved unit cost. For a pilot of 3 months, what's the recommended path? Dedicated reserved minimum or hosted with burst credits?
[03:40] Maya Chen: Two options: 1) Short pilot on Hosted with metered billing (easy, no commit). 2) Pilot on Dedicated with a small reserved pool — gives guaranteed latency and unit price discount. Because you care about latency predictability and region pinning, Dedicated is recommended. For 3 months we can do a short-term reserved rate (month-to-month commitment) or a trial credit applied to the first month. We'll put both on the pricing sheet.
[03:58] Jenna Morales: Is there a minimum spend for Dedicated?
[04:02] Maya Chen: Typically there is a minimal reserved capacity — for the pilot size you mentioned it would equate to approx $12k/month at list, but we can provide an adjusted pilot rate and credits. We'll include a breakdown (unit cost per 1k tokens, baseline vs burst).
[04:18] Tom Li: We will need the exact SLA numbers: p95 latency, uptime, and credits for not meeting SLOs. Procurement won't sign without explicit numbers.
[04:27] Rahul Patel: Our default Dedicated SLA states 99.9% availability for the serving nodes and p95 latency targets depend on model/seq length. For the chat model typical p95 is ~200-350ms on A100 class nodes at the sizes you're describing. We'll share the per-model benchmark doc.
[04:46] Priya Singh: We need to ensure fallback to a smaller model doesn't expose data to other tenants — is that handled?
[04:55] Maya Chen: Good question. For Dedicated pools with tenancy isolation, fallbacks stay within the same reserved pool. If using hosted fallback, requests could hit shared capacity; we can disable hosted fallback for your pilot to avoid that.
[05:07] Jenna Morales: Ok disable fallback.
[05:09] Tom Li: On the MSA redlines again — who will be the owner at Redwood for legal discussions?
[05:13] Maya Chen: I'll own the MSA/DPA orchestration. Legal will be looped in but I'll send the first pass redline with comments by Friday.
[05:20] Rahul Patel: Ops note — we'll need a sample prompt set and a synthetic load profile to validate latency. Can your team provide that?
[05:28] Jenna Morales: Yes, we can prepare a redacted prompt set and sample traffic profile; security will sign off on the redaction.
[05:34] Priya Singh: I'll review redactions. Also request: forward list of subprocessors and any SOC2 scope docs.
[05:42] Maya Chen: We'll attach SOC 2 Type II report and subprocessors list.
[05:46] Tom Li: Great. Quick question: do you support invoice net-60? Our finance prefers net-60.
[05:52] Maya Chen: Standard is net-30 but for pilots we can accommodate net-45 or net-60 with a purchase order. We'll note that for commercial.
[05:59] Rahul Patel: Operational fragility — for the pilot we recommend enabling prefix caching and an initial batch size config; that will reduce token cost and stabilize latency. We'll propose recommended settings in the runbook.
[06:12] Jenna Morales: Sounds good. Any blockers on your side?
[06:15] Maya Chen: No blockers. We need your procurement timeline and security requirements to finalize pricing and MSA/DPA.
[06:21] Tom Li: Procurement path: we have a two-step: internal procurement sign-off then finance approval; likely 7-10 business days once pricing is final.
[06:29] Priya Singh: Security will review the runbook and DPA redlines; I'll aim for feedback within 3 business days.
[06:35] Maya Chen: Perfect. Let's recap actions.
[06:38] Rahul Patel: I'll prepare the connectivity runbook, VPC checklist, and per-model latency benchmarks.
[06:43] Maya Chen: I'll produce the MSA/DPA redline summary and pilot pricing with dedicated vs hosted scenarios and credits. Also will include net-60 note.
[06:51] Jenna Morales: We'll produce the redacted prompt set and traffic profile.
[06:54] Tom Li: I'll confirm procurement path and PO template.
[06:58] Priya Singh: I'll send data class matrix and security checklist.
[07:02] Maya Chen: Great. Proposed follow-up: technical validation session next Wednesday (SE-led), legal redline by Friday, pilot kickoff provisioning the week of 2025-08-25 if approvals align.
[07:17] Tom Li: That schedule works tentatively.
[07:20] Jenna Morales: Yes. Thank you all.
[07:23] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and the artifacts.

End of transcript.

Recap (auto):
- Pilot: 3-month, region-pinned to eu-west-1, Dedicated recommended, no hosted fallback.
- Legal: MSA/DPA redlines to be circulated by Maya (due 2025-08-15).
- Tech: Rahul to deliver connectivity runbook and benchmark doc.
- Security: Priya to provide data-class matrix, retention reqs.
- Procurement: Tom to confirm PO/term preferences (net-60 ok).

References mentioned: pilot pricing sheet (link to be shared), MSA/DPA redline, SOC 2 Type II PDF, per-model benchmark spreadsheet, VPC connectivity checklist (all to be attached in follow-up email).
